rows.test: Conversation lists open with correct counts
rows.steps:
1. Log in as an agent.
2. Click Conversations in the left sidebar.
3. Click each tab at the top of the list in turn: Mine, Unassigned, All.
4. In the sidebar under Conversations, click Mentions, then Unattended.
5. For each, compare the number on the tab with the number of rows in the list.
6. Refresh the page and check All is selected and the status filter is All.
rows.dod: Each list loads in under 3 s. The count on each tab matches the conversations shown. All is the default tab and status filter.

rows.steps:
1. In the sidebar, expand Conversations.
2. Click one inbox under Inboxes (for example WhatsApp).
3. Click one team under Teams.
4. Click one label under Labels (for example dept_sales).
5. Open 3 conversations in each view and check they belong to that inbox, team or label.
rows.dod: Only conversations from that inbox, team or label are listed.

rows.test: Filter and save a custom view
rows.steps:
1. Log in as a supervisor and open Conversations.
2. Click the filter icon above the list.
3. Add filters: Status = Open, Priority = High, Labels = escalate, Created at = last 7 days. Click Apply filters.
4. Check every row matches all four filters.
5. Click Save filter, name it [TEST] Escalated high, and save.
6. Find the view under Folders in the sidebar, click away, then click it again to reopen.
rows.dod: Results match every filter. The saved view appears in the sidebar and reopens with the same filters.

rows.steps:
1. Open Conversations.
2. In the search box above the list, type a word from a recent message (for example servis) and press Enter.
3. Repeat with a contact name, then with a phone number.
4. Click one result and check the matching conversation opens at that message.
rows.dod: Matching conversations and messages are returned. Clicking a result opens that conversation.

rows.steps:
1. Log in as an agent who is a member of the WhatsApp inbox and set status Online.
2. From the test phone, send to the Proton WhatsApp number: [TEST] Hi, I want to book a service for my X50.
3. Start a stopwatch when you press send.
4. Check the conversation appears in Conversations > WhatsApp inbox within 10 s.
5. Check the contact name and phone number on the conversation.
6. Check the toast pops up and the alert sound plays.
rows.dod: Conversation appears in the WhatsApp inbox within 10 s with the contact's name and number. The inbound toast and sound fire for the agent.

rows.steps:
1. From the external test mailbox, email the E.Mas Centre address.
2. Subject: [TEST] Brake noise X70. Body: two lines of text. Attach a small JPG.
3. In the CRM open Conversations > the Email inbox.
4. Check the conversation appears within 2 minutes.
5. Open it and check subject, body and the image attachment.
rows.dod: Conversation appears in the Email inbox within 2 min. Subject, body and attachment are intact.
rows.knownIssue: Email inbox IMAP/SMTP not working (5 Nov audit). Fix before testing.

rows.steps:
1. Open the [TEST] WhatsApp conversation.
2. Make sure the Reply tab (not Private Note) is selected in the reply box.
3. Type: [TEST] Thank you, we will call you shortly. Press Send.
4. Check the test phone receives it and the message shows as sent (no red error icon).
5. Repeat on the [TEST] email conversation and check the reply lands in the same email thread in the test mailbox.
rows.dod: The customer receives the reply on the same channel and email thread. The message shows as sent with no error.
rows.knownIssue: Email part depends on the email inbox fix.

rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation.
2. Click the Private Note tab in the reply box (the box turns yellow).
3. Type @ and pick another test agent, then add: please check this case.
4. Press Add note.
5. Check the test phone received nothing.
6. Log in as the mentioned agent in Window B: check the bell notification and that the conversation is in Mentions.
rows.dod: The customer receives nothing. The mentioned agent gets a notification and the conversation appears in their Mentions list.

rows.test: Attach a file and insert a canned response
rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation, Reply tab.
2. Click the paperclip icon and attach one image and one PDF. Press Send.
3. Check both arrive on the test phone and open.
4. In the reply box type / and start typing a canned response name.
5. Pick it, check the text is inserted and any {{contact.name}} is replaced with the real name.
rows.dod: Files are delivered and can be previewed. The canned text is inserted with its variables filled in.

rows.test: Bot drafts the reply as a private note
rows.steps:
1. Make sure the WhatsApp inbox AI mode is Suggest (Knowledge > Inboxes).
2. From the test phone, start a new chat: [TEST] Berapa harga servis 10,000 km untuk X50?
3. Open the new conversation in the CRM.
4. Within about 30 s check a yellow private note with the suggested reply appears.
5. Check the test phone did not receive the AI reply.
6. Check the conversation status is Open, waiting for an agent.
rows.dod: Within about 30 s a private note with the suggested reply appears. Nothing is sent to the customer. The conversation is open for a human.
rows.knownIssue: Proton runs AGENT_MODE=auto (audit), so replies go straight to the customer. Decide suggest or auto first.

rows.test: Suggest reply, rewrite and Ask Copilot
rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation with a customer question.
2. Click the Copilot button above the reply box and choose suggest reply.
3. Check a draft appears in the reply box and can be edited.
4. Select the draft and use each rewrite action (for example shorter, more formal).
5. Open the Copilot panel, type in Ask about this conversation…: what is the customer asking? Press Enter.
6. Check the answer matches the thread and no error message shows.
rows.dod: A relevant draft appears in the composer and can be edited. Rewrites change tone without changing facts. No 401 or 500 errors.

rows.test: Translate EN, BM, ZH and TA
rows.steps:
1. Open a conversation whose last customer message is in Bahasa Malaysia.
2. Click Translate above the reply box and pick English.
3. Check the translation appears within 5 s and the original message is still visible.
4. Repeat for Chinese and Tamil.
5. Write a draft reply in English and translate it to BM and ZH.
6. If you see Translation failed. Please try again., note it as Fail.
rows.dod: Each translation returns within 5 s and the original text is kept.
rows.knownIssue: Tamil works for reading inbound messages only; outbound Tamil replies are not supported (audit).

rows.steps:
1. Check Knowledge > FAQs has an FAQ about service booking.
2. From the test phone send: [TEST] How do I book a service?
3. Open the conversation and look at the FAQ strip above the reply box.
4. Check the service booking FAQ is listed.
5. Click Apply and check its answer is placed in the reply box (not sent).
rows.dod: Matching FAQs show in the strip. Apply puts the FAQ answer into the composer.

rows.steps:
1. Log in as a supervisor and open a [TEST] conversation.
2. In the right panel under Conversation Actions, set Assigned agent to a test agent.
3. Set Assigned team to a test team and Priority to High.
4. Check the assignee shows in the list and the conversation header.
5. Check the activity line (for example assigned to …) appears in the thread.
6. Log in as that agent and check the notification.
rows.dod: Assignee shows in the list and the header. The assignee is notified. An activity message is logged.

rows.steps:
1. Prepare 3 test agents in the WhatsApp inbox: A Online, B Busy, C Offline (My status).
2. From the test phone send a new message: [TEST] routing check.
3. Open the new conversation and check it was assigned to agent A.
4. Set A to Busy and send another new message from a second test number.
5. Check it stays unassigned or goes to the next Online agent, never to B or C.
rows.dod: The new conversation goes only to an Online agent, following the channel priority.
rows.knownIssue: Firestore presence index missing (audit).

rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation.
2. In the right panel under Labels, click the edit icon and add two labels (for example dept_sales and vip).
3. Remove one of them.
4. Check the remaining label shows on the conversation and in the list row.
5. Click the label in the sidebar and check the conversation is listed.
rows.dod: Labels show on the conversation and in the list. Filtering by the label finds the conversation.

rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation.
2. Click the arrow next to Resolve and choose Snooze > Until tomorrow.
3. Check it leaves the Open list and appears under Snoozed.
4. Open it and click Resolve. Check it is under Resolved.
5. From the test phone send a new message in the same chat.
6. Check the conversation is Open again.
rows.dod: Snoozed conversation leaves Open until the snooze time. Resolved moves to Resolved. The customer message reopens it.

rows.test: AI fills case taxonomy, agent can correct it
rows.steps:
1. Open the [TEST] conversation created in CONV-005 after the AI has replied or drafted.
2. In the right panel open Conversation information.
3. Check case_type, case_category, case_subcategory, case_detail and vehicle_model are filled.
4. Change case_category with the dropdown; check the subcategory list changes to match.
5. Refresh the page and check your change was kept.
rows.dod: case_type, case_category, case_subcategory, case_detail and vehicle_model are filled. The agent's change saves and stays after refresh.

rows.steps:
1. Open a conversation from a returning customer.
2. In the right panel, find the DMS card.
3. Check it shows vehicle data or a clear not-connected message (no spinning or blank card).
4. Scroll to Previous Conversations and check older chats are listed and open when clicked.
rows.dod: The DMS card loads or shows a clear not-connected message. Previous conversations are listed.

rows.steps:
1. From the external test mailbox, email: [TEST] My car makes noise after the last service at the dealer.
2. Open the new email conversation.
3. Within about 30 s check a private note suggests a department (for example dept_aftersales).
4. Do not apply it yet; note the suggestion in Evidence.
rows.dod: A private note suggests the department label to apply.
rows.knownIssue: Depends on the email inbox fix.

rows.steps:
1. Check Escalation Routing has a PIC email (a Devoteam test mailbox) for the department you will use.
2. Open the [TEST] email conversation.
3. In Labels add the department label (for example dept_sales). Then add escalate.
4. Start a stopwatch.
5. Within about 15 s check the customer test mailbox gets an acknowledgement email.
6. Check the PIC test mailbox gets a forward whose Reply-To contains +case<conversation id>.
7. In Conversation information check escalation_notified_at has a time.
rows.dod: Within about 15 s two emails go out: an acknowledgement to the customer and a forward to the PIC with a +case<id> Reply-To. escalation_notified_at is stamped.
rows.knownIssue: Email inbox IMAP/SMTP not working (5 Nov audit). Fix before testing. Departments without a PIC email nobody.

rows.test: PIC reply links back to the case
rows.steps:
1. In the PIC test mailbox, open the forward from ESC test.
2. Click Reply (keep the Reply-To address) and write: [TEST] PIC reply, part ordered, ETA 3 days. Send.
3. In the CRM, open the case and wait up to 40 s.
4. Check the reply shows as a private note.
5. Check an AI draft reply for the customer appears.
6. Check the escalation_replied label was added.
rows.dod: Within about 40 s the reply shows as a private note, an AI draft for the customer appears and the escalation_replied label is added.
rows.knownIssue: Depends on the email inbox fix.

rows.steps:
1. Check the test dealer in Escalation Routing has Devoteam test addresses for every ladder contact.
2. On a [TEST] email case add the dealer_<slug> label, then escalate.
3. Check dealer_escalated_at is stamped in Conversation information.
4. Check the CRE and Sales/AS Manager test mailboxes get step 1, with Principal, ARM and HOD in CC.
5. Reply from the CRE test mailbox.
6. Check the case gets escalation_replied and no step 3 reminder is sent later.
7. Resolve the case when done.
rows.dod: dealer_escalated_at is stamped. Step 1 emails CRE and Sales/AS Manager with Principal, ARM and HOD in CC. Reminders stop after the dealer reply.
rows.knownIssue: Ladder is live (dry run off). Resolve the test case afterwards so no reminders go out.

rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation with a phone number.
2. Click the call icon and allow the microphone when the browser asks.
3. Answer on the test phone and speak both ways. Click Mute, then Unmute.
4. Hang up and check Call ended shows and the call is logged on the conversation.
5. Call the agent number from the test phone and check Incoming call shows; answer it.
rows.dod: The call connects with audio both ways and is logged on the conversation.
rows.knownIssue: Only if the softphone feature is on.

rows.steps:
1. Note the welcome, inactivity and resolution texts in Knowledge > Settings.
2. From the test phone start a new chat: [TEST] hello.
3. Check the welcome message arrives once.
4. Do not reply; wait past the inactivity time set on the inbox. Check the inactivity message arrives once.
5. In the CRM click Resolve. Check the resolution message arrives once.
rows.dod: Each configured message is sent once, at the configured time.

rows.steps:
1. Check CSAT is on for the WhatsApp inbox (Settings > Inboxes > WhatsApp > CSAT).
2. Resolve a [TEST] WhatsApp conversation.
3. On the test phone, open the survey and give 5 stars with comment [TEST].
4. Open Reports > CSAT and check the rating is listed.
rows.dod: The customer receives the survey and the rating shows in the CSAT report.

rows.steps:
1. Open Settings > Inboxes and look for a Messenger and an Instagram inbox.
2. From a test Facebook account, send [TEST] hello to the Proton page.
3. From a test Instagram account, send [TEST] hello as a DM.
4. Check both arrive as conversations in their inbox.
rows.dod: Both messages arrive as conversations in the shared conversation list, next to WhatsApp and email.
rows.knownIssue: No Messenger or Instagram inbox is connected on proton today. Needs Meta page access from Proton.

rows.steps:
1. From the test phone send a 15 MB video and an .xlsx file on WhatsApp.
2. From the test mailbox send a 20 MB PDF and a .zip.
3. Open each conversation and download every file.
rows.dod: Every file arrives and opens. Any file refused is refused by the channel's own limit (WhatsApp media is capped at 16 MB by Meta), with an error the agent can see.
rows.knownIssue: Channel providers set hard size limits; record the actual limit you hit.

rows.steps:
1. From the test phone send a voice note, a photo of a dashboard warning light and a 10 s video.
2. Open the conversation.
3. Play the voice note and video, open the photo.
4. Click Copilot suggest reply.
rows.dod: All media plays or opens in the conversation. The suggested reply refers to what is in the photo.

rows.steps:
1. Open a [TEST] conversation with at least 6 messages.
2. Click Copilot and choose Summarize.
3. Read the summary.
rows.dod: The summary is in English and covers the customer's issue, what was done and the outcome.
rows.knownIssue: Automatic summary on resolve is off (AUTO_SUMMARY_ON_RESOLVE_ENABLED). Manual Summarize only.

rows.steps:
1. Create a [TEST] contact with email nobody@invalid-domain-test.example.
2. Start an email conversation to that contact and send a reply.
3. Wait 2 minutes and check the conversation.
rows.dod: A note or alert tells the agent the email bounced or the address is invalid.
rows.knownIssue: Email inbox IMAP/SMTP not working (5 Nov audit). Fix before testing. BOUNCE_HANDLING_ENABLED is on; the escalation failure note is off.

rows.steps:
1. Check the WhatsApp inbox business hours (Settings > Inboxes > WhatsApp > Business Hours).
2. Send a message from the test phone outside those hours.
3. Open the conversation and check its attributes and labels.
rows.dod: The out-of-office reply is sent, and the conversation is marked as received after hours so reports can count it.
rows.knownIssue: Working-hours SLA is off (SLA_WORKING_HOURS_ENABLED). Check where the after-hours mark is stored.

rows.test: AI understands short forms and slang
rows.steps:
1. From the test phone send: brp lama siap? nk service
2. Then: kete sy rosak kat highway, tlg
3. Open the conversation and read the AI reply or draft.
rows.dod: The AI reads the first as asking how long a service takes and the second as a breakdown, and answers each correctly.

rows.test: Second enquiry from the same customer
rows.steps:
1. From the test phone open a case about brake noise and resolve it.
2. Send a new message about the same brake noise.
3. Open the new conversation and the contact panel.
rows.dod: The agent sees the earlier case under Previous Conversations and can link or merge. Record whether anything was merged automatically.
rows.knownIssue: AI duplicate detection and auto-merge (RFP 4.25) is not built. Only manual contact merge exists.

rows.steps:
1. Call the Proton number from the test phone.
2. Say: my car broke down on the highway, I need a tow.
3. Hang up and call again. Say: I want to speak to an agent.
rows.dod: The first call goes to the RSA route, the second to a live agent. Each call creates a conversation in the phone inbox.

rows.test: AI answers calls in four languages
rows.steps:
1. Call and ask about service booking in Bahasa Malaysia.
2. Call again in English, then Chinese, then Tamil.
rows.dod: The AI answers in the language the caller used each time and hands off when asked.
rows.knownIssue: Tamil quality not yet evaluated.

rows.steps:
1. Call and get handed to an agent.
2. Watch the agent's screen while you talk in BM and English.
rows.dod: Text appears on the agent's screen during the call, in the language spoken.

rows.steps:
1. Answer a test call on the softphone.
2. Click Mute, then Unmute.
3. Put the call on hold and listen on the test phone.
4. Transfer the call to a second agent.
rows.dod: Mute works both ways, hold plays the hold recording, and the second agent receives the call with the case.
rows.knownIssue: Hold with recording and transfer: check they exist in the softphone; record if missing.

rows.steps:
1. After a test call, open its conversation.
2. Play the recording and open its transcript.
rows.dod: The recording plays and the transcript is attached to the case.

rows.steps:
1. Call and talk to the AI.
2. Say: saya nak cakap dengan orang.
rows.dod: The call moves to an agent's softphone with the conversation so far.

rows.steps:
1. Call outside business hours.
2. Listen to the message, leave a voicemail.
3. Call again and say it is a breakdown.
rows.dod: An after-hours message plays, the voicemail becomes a case, and the breakdown call still reaches RSA.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (PHONE_AFTER_HOURS_ENABLED, PHONE_VOICEMAIL_INGEST_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A.

rows.test: Caller rates the agent after the call
rows.steps:
1. At the end of a call, the agent sends the caller to the rating.
2. Rate 9 on the keypad or by voice.
rows.dod: The rating is saved against the agent.
rows.knownIssue: NPS survey is not running on proton.

rows.test: Dropped calls in the queue are counted
rows.steps:
1. Call while all agents are busy.
2. Hang up while waiting.
3. Open the call report.
rows.dod: The call is counted as abandoned.
rows.knownIssue: Check the abandon report exists; record if missing.

rows.test: Create, edit and delete an assistant
rows.steps:
1. Log in as admin. Click Knowledge > Assistants.
2. Click the add button. Name: [TEST] Assistant, Description: test only. Save.
3. Edit the name to [TEST] Assistant 2 and save. Refresh.
4. Delete the test assistant from the Actions column and confirm it is gone.
rows.dod: Each change saves and stays after refresh.

rows.test: Add, edit and delete an FAQ
rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > FAQs and click the add button.
2. Question: [TEST] Where is the nearest service centre? Answer: use the dealer locator on proton.com. Keywords: service, centre. Save.
3. Edit the answer, save, refresh, and check the edit stayed.
4. Delete the FAQ.
5. From the test phone ask the same question and check the FAQ strip no longer shows it.
rows.dod: Changes stay after refresh. A deleted FAQ is no longer suggested in conversations.

rows.steps:
1. Create test.csv with columns question,answer,keywords and 5 rows starting with [TEST].
2. Knowledge > FAQs > Bulk upload (CSV), pick test.csv.
3. Check the success message shows 5 rows imported and they appear in the list.
4. Make bad.csv with the answer column removed and upload it.
5. Check an error names the missing column and no new rows appear.
6. Delete the 5 test FAQs.
rows.dod: The valid file imports all 5 rows and shows the count. The bad file shows an error naming the problem and imports nothing.

rows.test: Upload, list and delete a document
rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > Documents and upload a small PDF named [TEST] brochure.pdf.
2. Wait until its status shows ready.
3. Use Filter by title, URL, snippet… to find it.
4. Delete it and check it is gone.
5. Open the old document URL and check a message appears, not a blank page.
rows.dod: The document is listed with its status. After delete it is gone. A missing document shows a message, not a blank page.

rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > Scenarios and click the add button.
2. Title: [TEST] Warranty claim handling. Description: test only. Save.
3. Edit the description and save. Refresh and check it stayed.
4. Delete the test scenario.
rows.dod: The scenario saves and stays after refresh.

rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > Tools > Custom tools and click the add button.
2. Name: [TEST] Check order status, Method: GET, Endpoint: a test URL. Save.
3. Edit the description and save. Refresh and check it stayed.
4. Delete the test tool.
rows.dod: The tool saves and stays after refresh.

rows.test: Answers come from the knowledge base
rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > Playground and pick the Proton assistant.
2. In Ask the assistant something… type a question from an existing FAQ (for example warranty period for X50).
3. Check the answer matches the FAQ text.
4. Ask something not in the KB (for example the price of a Ferrari).
5. Check the assistant says it does not know or offers a human, and invents nothing.
rows.dod: The first answer uses the FAQ or document content. The second hands off or says it does not know, with no made-up answer.

rows.test: Map an assistant to an inbox
rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > Inboxes.
2. Find the WhatsApp inbox row and set Assistant to the Proton assistant and Mode to Suggest.
3. Save, refresh, and check the values stayed.
4. Send a test message and check the draft note uses this assistant's tone.
rows.dod: The mapping saves. The bot on that inbox uses this assistant's persona.

rows.steps:
1. Click Knowledge > Settings and pick the Proton assistant.
2. In the instructions add: End every reply with Terima kasih, Proton e.MAS. Save.
3. From the test phone send a new question.
4. Check the AI draft or reply ends with that line.
5. Remove the line, save, and check the next reply goes back to normal.
rows.dod: Settings stay after refresh and the next bot reply follows the change.

rows.test: Welcome, handoff, resolution and lifecycle messages
rows.steps:
1. In Knowledge > Settings, edit the welcome, handoff and resolution messages, starting each with [TEST].
2. Save.
3. Start a chat from the test phone and check the [TEST] welcome arrives.
4. Ask for a human and check the [TEST] handoff message.
5. Resolve and check the [TEST] resolution message.
6. Restore the original texts and save.
rows.dod: The customer receives the edited text.

rows.steps:
1. In Knowledge > Settings open the email templates.
2. Add [TEST] to the acknowledgement subject. Save.
3. Run the CONV-021 escalation.
4. Check the acknowledgement email subject starts with [TEST].
5. Restore the template.
rows.dod: The escalation emails use the edited template.
rows.knownIssue: Depends on the email inbox fix.

rows.steps:
1. Open a conversation where the FAQ strip shows a suggestion.
2. Use the rating or feedback control on the suggestion.
3. As admin, open Knowledge > FAQs and look for the rating.
rows.dod: The agent's rating is saved and visible to the admin against that FAQ.
rows.knownIssue: Check the rating control exists on the strip; record if missing.

rows.steps:
1. Ask the bot 3 questions that have no FAQ.
2. As admin, look for a list of unanswered or suggested FAQ topics.
rows.dod: The admin can see the unanswered topics and add an FAQ from them.
rows.knownIssue: Not built as a screen (RFP 4.56 item 8). Record as N/A unless found.

rows.test: Bot answers at night and hands off
rows.steps:
1. At night, send a question covered by an FAQ.
2. Then ask something complex: my car was repaired 3 times and still fails, I want compensation.
rows.dod: The FAQ question is answered. The complex one is handed to a human with the conversation open for the morning shift.
rows.knownIssue: AGENT_MODE=auto on proton: replies go straight to the customer.

rows.test: Angry or urgent messages are flagged
rows.steps:
1. Send: This is the third time! Nobody helps me, I am very angry.
2. Send: Kereta mati tengah jalan, anak saya dalam kereta.
rows.dod: The first is flagged dissatisfied, the second urgent, and the reply tone adjusts.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (SENTIMENT_CLASSIFIER_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A.

rows.test: AI reads a photo and asks the right question
rows.steps:
1. Send a photo of a warning light on the dashboard.
2. Read the AI reply or draft.
rows.dod: The AI names the likely issue and asks a relevant follow-up question.
rows.knownIssue: Photo/video diagnosis has not been tried on a real customer image yet.

rows.test: Suggestions use KB and past resolved cases
rows.steps:
1. Open a conversation similar to a resolved [TEST] case.
2. Click Copilot suggest reply.
rows.dod: The draft uses FAQ content and, where relevant, how the earlier case was solved.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (RESOLVED_CASE_INDEX_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A.

rows.steps:
1. As admin, look for a view listing every conversation the AI is handling now.
2. Use Reports > Bot and a bot-handled filter as a fallback.
rows.dod: The admin can see live AI conversations in one place.
rows.knownIssue: No dedicated AI activity page was built (RFP 3.2.5).

rows.steps:
1. Write a reply and translate it to Tamil.
2. Send it.
rows.dod: The Tamil reply is sent.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (TRANSLATION_OUTBOUND_TAMIL_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A. Returns 403 today.

rows.test: AI usage is counted per conversation
rows.steps: 1. Open the AI cost or usage report.
rows.dod: Token or call usage is shown per day and per conversation.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (TOKEN_METERING_ENABLED, AI_COST_REPORTING_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A.

rows.test: AI taxonomy matches the agent's judgement
rows.steps:
1. Pick 10 recent conversations.
2. For each, compare the AI case category with what the agent would choose.
3. Record how many match.
rows.dod: At least 8 of 10 match (or the target Proton agrees).
rows.knownIssue: Human Resolve does not trigger auto-categorise (audit).

rows.steps:
1. Log in as admin. Click SLA Policies in the sidebar.
2. Create a policy [TEST] SLA with first response 15 min and resolution 4 h.
3. Save and check the SLA policy saved. message.
4. Edit the resolution to 8 h, save, refresh, and check it stayed.
rows.dod: The policy and its thresholds save and are listed.

rows.test: Policy applies to the right inboxes
rows.steps:
1. On SLA Policies check the Scope includes the live WhatsApp and Email inboxes.
2. Send a new message from the test phone.
3. Open the conversation and check an SLA timer is shown.
4. If there is no timer, mark Blocked (scope still on deleted inbox 4).
rows.dod: The SLA timer shows on the conversation.
rows.knownIssue: SLA_INBOX_IDS still points at deleted inbox 4 (audit).

rows.steps:
1. Use a [TEST] conversation in a scoped inbox and do not reply.
2. Wait until the warning threshold.
3. Check one warning note or alert appears on the conversation.
4. Check no second warning is posted for the same threshold.

3. Log in as the test agent in Window B.
4. Change their role to Administrator, then back.
5. Deactivate the agent and check they can no longer log in.
rows.dod: The agent can log in after setup. A deactivated agent cannot log in.
rows.knownIssue: No SMTP for invites: set the password in super admin.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Teams > Create new team: [TEST] Team.
2. Add two test agents and save.
3. Assign a [TEST] conversation to the team and check it shows under the team in the sidebar.
rows.dod: The team saves and the conversation shows under the team.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Inboxes > WhatsApp.
2. Check the Settings, Collaborators and Configuration tabs open and show the right members.
3. Send a test message and check it arrives.
rows.dod: Settings save and the message arrives.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Inboxes > Email > Configuration.
2. Check IMAP and SMTP are enabled and the connection shows no error.
3. Send a test email in (CONV-006) and reply out (CONV-007).
rows.dod: Both directions work.
rows.knownIssue: Email inbox IMAP/SMTP not working (5 Nov audit). Fix before testing.

rows.test: Business hours, greeting, CSAT and inactivity timing
rows.steps:
1. Settings > Inboxes > WhatsApp > Business Hours.
2. Set hours that exclude now and add an out-of-office message starting with [TEST]. Save.
3. Message from the test phone and check the out-of-office message arrives.
4. Check greeting, CSAT and inactivity settings save.
5. Restore the original hours.
rows.dod: The out-of-office message is sent. Greeting, CSAT and inactivity settings save.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Labels.
2. Check these exist: every dept_*, every dealer_*, escalate and escalation_replied.
3. List any missing in Evidence.
rows.dod: dept_*, dealer_*, escalate and escalation_replied labels all exist.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Custom Attributes > Conversation.
2. Check case_type, case_category, case_subcategory, case_detail, vehicle_model, escalation_notified_at and dealer_escalated_at exist.
3. Check each has the expected type (list or text, date).
rows.dod: Taxonomy attributes, the escalation_* attributes and dealer_escalated_at exist with the right types.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Automation > Add Automation Rule: [TEST] rule, when a conversation is created with message containing autotest, add label vip.
2. Send autotest from the test phone and check the label is added once.
3. Delete the test rule.
4. Check rule 2 is still disabled.
rows.dod: The test rule fires once. Rule 2 stays disabled.
rows.knownIssue: Keep automation rule 2 disabled.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Agent Bots.
2. Check the bot is connected to the right inboxes.
3. Send a test message and check the bot responds there and not in other inboxes.
rows.dod: The bot responds on the attached inboxes only.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Macros > Add macro: [TEST] macro that adds a label and assigns a team.
2. Run it from the macros button on a [TEST] conversation.
3. Check both actions happened, then delete the macro.
rows.dod: Every action in the macro is applied.

rows.steps:
1. Settings > Canned Responses > Add: short code testcr, content [TEST] Hello {{contact.name}}.
2. In a conversation type /testcr and insert it.
3. Check the name is filled in, then delete the canned response.
rows.dod: It can be found with / and is inserted correctly.

rows.steps:
1. Open the agent priorities page.
2. Change the channel order (for example WhatsApp above Email) and save.
3. Refresh and check the order stayed.
4. Send one WhatsApp and one email at the same time and check which is assigned first.
rows.dod: The order saves and new conversations are routed in that order.

rows.steps:
1. Open Integrations.
2. For each webhook send a test delivery and check it succeeds.
3. On DMS / TSP check Base URL and Auth type are set (do not show the credential).
4. Check connected apps show as connected.
rows.dod: Each webhook test returns success. Connected apps show as connected.

rows.steps:
1. Set business hours on the scoped inbox.
2. Create a [TEST] case 30 minutes before closing and leave it overnight.
3. Check the SLA timer the next morning.
rows.dod: The timer paused outside working hours.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (SLA_WORKING_HOURS_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A.

rows.steps:
1. Log out, log in with a test user.
2. Click Forgot password? and enter the test user's email.
rows.dod: Login works. The reset email arrives.
rows.knownIssue: No SMTP for system email on proton, so the reset email may not send.

rows.steps:
1. Open Profile settings and look for two-factor authentication.
2. Turn it on with an authenticator app, log out and back in.
rows.dod: Login asks for the code and works with it.
rows.knownIssue: Check the option is visible; patch 0032 hid the Security settings menu.

rows.steps:
1. Look for a password expiry setting.
2. Change your own password from Profile.
rows.dod: Self-service change works. Expiry after 3 months is enforced.
rows.knownIssue: Expiry prompt is not built.

rows.steps:
1. Log in and leave the browser idle past the agreed timeout.
2. Click anything.
rows.dod: The user is asked to log in again.
rows.knownIssue: Record the actual timeout.

rows.steps:
1. Open a conversation with a phone number and IC number in a message.
2. Check how they show to an agent without full access.
rows.dod: Sensitive numbers are masked for roles that should not see them.
rows.knownIssue: Not built; only a prompt-level mitigation exists.

rows.test: Users only see their own data scope
rows.steps:
1. Give a test role access to one team's conversations only.
2. Log in as that user.
rows.dod: Only that team's conversations and reports are visible.
rows.knownIssue: Built, but switched off on proton (DATA_SCOPED_RBAC_ENABLED). Turn it on in the tenant env first, or mark N/A.

rows.steps:
1. Check the retention settings for conversations, audit log and recordings.
2. Check purge jobs are off or set to 7 years.
rows.dod: Nothing is deleted before 7 years.
rows.knownIssue: Audit and recording purge jobs are off; confirm the written retention policy.

rows.test: Backups exist and can be restored
rows.steps:
1. Check the VM disk snapshot schedule and the database backup schedule in GCP.
2. Restore last night's backup to a test instance.
rows.dod: A backup from the last 24 hours exists and restores cleanly.
rows.knownIssue: Not checked in the audit. Verify before go-live.

rows.steps:
1. Check GCP uptime checks and alert policies for the CRM URL.
2. Stop nothing on prod; review the last 30 days of uptime.
rows.dod: An uptime check and an alert to the support team exist.
rows.knownIssue: Not checked in the audit.

rows.steps:
1. Log in as admin.
2. Click every sidebar item from Conversations to Settings.
3. Check each page opens with no permission error.
rows.dod: Every module opens with no permission error.

rows.test: Supervisor sees operations, not admin settings
rows.steps:
1. Log in as a supervisor.
2. Click every sidebar item.
3. Check Conversations, Reports, Workforce and Customer 360 open, and admin pages (Roles & Permissions, Custom features) are not shown.
rows.dod: Conversations, Reports, Workforce and Customer 360 open. Admin-only pages are hidden.

rows.steps:
1. Log in as an agent.
2. Check only Conversations, Contacts, My status and Alert preferences are in the sidebar.
3. Note any extra item in Evidence.
rows.dod: Only Conversations, Contacts, My status and Alert preferences are available. Other pages are hidden.

rows.test: Hidden pages cannot be opened by URL
rows.steps:
1. As admin copy the URLs of SLA Policies, Roles & Permissions and Escalation Routing.
2. Log in as an agent and paste each URL.
3. Check each is refused or redirected and no data shows.
rows.dod: Each URL is blocked or redirects. No data is shown.
